after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed to the owner as a paper strategy of its own (rule 14), on the broker's USD pairs, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.data: Yahoo daily closes (units per dollar, dated by the source's own calendar); the BIS WS_CBPOL bulk file, its daily rows for the seven areas; each file's sha256 in the manifest

gates.costs_x2: mean monthly net > 0 with the spreads and the markup doubled
gates.leave_one_out: the rule run without any one of the six currencies still earns a mean monthly net > 0
gates.t: t of the mean monthly net return of the carry book, 2005-02..2019-12, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total net

spec.holdout_rule: 2020-01..2026-09: mean monthly net > 0 with one-sided t >= 1.645, and > 0 with the spreads and the markup doubled
spec.question: does holding the three highest-yielding of six emerging currencies against the dollar, monthly, earn a positive net return after a CFD's costs?
spec.rule: at each month's last close common to all six, rank by policy-rate differential against the Fed (BIS WS_CBPOL, in force that day); hold the top three, a third each, long against the dollar, to the next common month-end; earn the spot move and the differential by calendar days; pay the markup on what is held and each spread on what is traded
